section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header of the maamar, including the Torah portion, date, and year.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Torah portion of Pinchas,
16 Tammuz,

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the division of the Land of Israel was by lot, by Divine inspiration, and also by intellect according to population size.
section.t: "But you shall divide the land by lot"¹,
the division of the Holy Land,
which they conquered the land of Canaan²
and made it the Land of Israel,
and even while the Children of Israel were still in the desert
(before they came to the Land of Israel)
it was said about it "a land which... the eyes of the L-rd your G-d are upon it from the beginning of the year until the end of the year"³,
behold it is explained that the division of the Holy Land was by means of the lot.
And there was an addition to this "according to the word of the L-rd"⁴
and Rashi explains⁵
[it was] with the Holy Spirit.
And there was another matter in the division of the land: "to the large [tribe] you shall increase its inheritance, and to the small you shall diminish its inheritance"⁶,
which is a matter according to intellect.
For the simple explanation of "to the large you shall increase etc." is as Rashi explains
[for Rashi's commentary on the Torah is the plain meaning of the verse⁷]
to a tribe that was numerous in population they gave a large portion, for the portions were not equal, etc.,
for this division is according to intellect.
[And although the Ramban disagrees with this, and there are other interpretations in Rashi⁸,
nevertheless the Ramban explains Rashi's intention as the simple meaning.
And even according to the Ramban, and according to these commentators who explain Rashi's words like the opinion of the Ramban,
behold from this very fact that according to their interpretation the verse needed to negate division according to intellect, it proves that this division has a connection to intellect.
But the main discussion here is the plain meaning of the verse and the plain meaning of Rashi's commentary and the Sifri⁹.
That the division was according to the number of people,
which is a division according to intellect].
Thus we find that in the division of the land there were three matters:
by lot,
by the Holy Spirit,
and by intellect, which is also understood in the intellectual soul.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the concept of division by lot relates to the essence of the soul, beyond intellect and emotion, as explained by the Tzemach Tzedek based on the Alter Rebbe.
section.t: Now, the matter of the division of the land by lot is explained by his holy honor, the Tzemach Tzedek¹⁰,
based on the discourse of his holy honor, the Alter Rebbe¹¹
regarding what Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said: "I do not know on which path they are leading me"¹²,
for at first glance this is perplexing,
for Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai never walked four cubits without Torah and without tefillin¹³,
and for eighty years he learned and taught Torah¹⁴
etc.,
so what room is there for doubt about which path they are leading him?
And his holy honor, the Alter Rebbe, explains regarding this that this is from the aspect of the essence of the soul,
that is, from the aspect of the level of the soul that is above intellect and emotion.
Therefore Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said "I do not know etc.",
even though he engaged in Torah etc.,
because this engagement in Torah is a matter that relates to intellect and emotion, and from this there is no proof regarding the level that is above intellect and emotion.
Now, also this level,
since there is in it the matter of reward and punishment
(as is understood from this very thing that Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said "I do not know on which path they are leading me"),
it is proven from this
that there is possibility, ability, and permission given to every person¹⁵
also regarding this level in the soul.
That is, there is such an avodah (divine service) that also affects the essence of the soul, and through it it will be as it should be¹⁶.
And this level in the soul,
and also the avodah that relates to this level,
is called by the name "lot" (goral)¹⁷.
And based on this, the Tzemach Tzedek explains the matter of the division of the land by lot.
